facts.text: The study compared laser-assisted machining (LAM) with conventional machining (CM) of the same DED-fabricated Ti33Nb28Cr11V11Ni alloy.
LAM used laser preheating ahead of a TiAlN + SH-coated flat-end mill at 100 mm/min feed, 0.3 mm cutting depth, and 3 mm laser-to-tool separation.
The LAM process produced an approximately 930 °C surface temperature and about 800 °C at the 0.3 mm cutting depth.
High-temperature tensile behavior was measured from 22 to 1000 °C, and thermal properties were measured under argon up to 1000 °C.
Laser preheating brought the cutting layer into the strong-softening regime at approximately 800 °C or above, reducing workpiece strength and cutting resistance before material removal.
LAM caused less machining-induced grain refinement than CM, leaving a post-machining grain size of 3.18 μm rather than 2.20 μm.
LAM reduced the resultant cutting force relative to CM.
The cutting-force reduction with LAM was 60.0% relative to CM.
LAM improved surface roughness relative to CM.
The surface-roughness improvement with LAM was 41.4% relative to CM.
LAM produced less machining-induced work hardening than CM.
Hardness increased by only 1.48% after LAM, compared with a 4.98% increase after CM.
